references.text: Solomon's proverbs warn against pushing oneself forward among the great and encourage humility: "Do not boast in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of the great! For it is better to be told, 'Come up here!' than to be humbled before a prince." Jesus' parable in [ref:Luk 14:8-10|Luke 14:8-10] appears to build directly on this wisdom tradition from [ref:Ordsp 25:6-7|Proverbs 25:6-7].

The direct continuation of Jesus' parable, where he explains the point about choosing the lowest place at the table so that the host may invite you to move up. The parable culminates with the principle: "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted" ([ref:Luk 14:8-11|Luke 14:8-11]).

Jesus warns against the scribes who love the places of honor in the synagogues and the seats of distinction at banquets ([ref:Luk 20:46|Luke 20:46]). This connects to the same motif of seeking places of honor as in Luke 14:7.

Jesus criticizes the Pharisees and scribes because they "love the places of honor at banquets and the best seats in the synagogues" ([ref:Matt 23:6-7|Matthew 23:6-7]). The same theme of seeking the highest places that Jesus observes in [ref:Luk 14:7|Luke 14:7].

Also in the Gospel of Mark, Jesus warns against the scribes who desire the best seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets ([ref:Mark 12:38-39|Mark 12:38-39]), as a parallel to the theme in Luke 14:7.

Jesus pronounces a woe upon the Pharisees because they "love the best seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces" ([ref:Luk 11:43|Luke 11:43]). This shows the recurring theme of self-exaltation through seeking places of honor.

In the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector, the principle is repeated: "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted" ([ref:Luk 18:14|Luke 18:14]). The same principle of humility that underlies the parable in Luke 14.

James writes that "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble" ([ref:Jak 4:6|James 4:6]). This confirms the biblical principle of humility that Jesus illustrates with the parable in [ref:Luk 14:7|Luke 14:7].

Peter exhorts: "Clothe yourselves all with humility toward one another! For God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble" ([ref:1 Pet 5:5|1 Peter 5:5]). The same theme of humility that Jesus teaches in his parable about a banquet.
